'''Amrik Singh Nimbran''', retired [[Indian Police Service]] officer and amateur mathematician.

== Personal life ==
Amrik Singh Nimran was born into a [[Dalit]] family at Gurgaon, Haryana.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2015-01-12|title=Manjhi empowers Dalit IAS officers|url=https://www.tkbsen.in/2015/01/manjhi-empowers-dalit-ias-officers/|access-date=2020-06-07|website=The Sen Times|language=en-US}}</ref>

In 1992, he wrote ''Poverty, Land, and Violence: An Analytical Study of Naxalism in Bihar''.

== Civil services ==
Nimbran is a 1979-batch Indian Police Service officer of Bihar cadre.

He is the only IPS officer who has held every position in [[Patna district|Patna]]. He was SP, Senior SP, DIG Central Range, and I.G. (Patna Zone) and later appointed as DGP of Bihar (Fire Service and Home Guard).<ref>{{Cite web|date=December 7, 2014|title=Nimbran tipped to be security adviser to govt|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/patna/Nimbran-tipped-to-be-security-adviser-to-govt/articleshow/45399246.cms|access-date=2020-06-07|website=The Times of India|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|agency=Press Trust of India|date=2013-02-11|title=Bihar govt promotes four IPS officers to DGP rank|work=Business Standard India|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/pti-stories/bihar-govt-promotes-four-ips-officers-to-dgp-rank-113021200591_1.html|access-date=2020-06-07}}</ref>

He retired in 2014, after giving 35 years of service to the state.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Nimbran Retires; Thanks Bihar for Allowing it to Serve - PatnaDaily|url=https://www.patnadaily.com/index.php/news/9393-nimbran-retires-thanks-bihar-for-allowing-it-to-serve.html|access-date=2020-06-07|website=www.patnadaily.com}}</ref>

He is the first State Security Advisor of Bihar and included under [[Jitan Ram Manjhi]]'s government. Being a [[Dalit]] and senior officer, Nimbran was considered Majhi's comrade.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2015-01-11|title=Caste is his comrade: Manjhi wields Dalit officers to gain grip over Bihar|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india/caste-is-his-comrade-manjhi-wields-dalit-officers-to-gain-grip-over-bihar/story-2EOIU3YRaAFpJayLwExllJ.html|access-date=2020-06-07|website=Hindustan Times|language=en}}</ref>

== Mathematics ==
He is an amateur mathematician and his papers have been published in the ''[[Indian Journal of Pure and Applied Mathematics]]'' and Indian Math Society in 2016 and ''[[The Ramanujan Journal]]'' in 2018 regarding Generalized Wallis-Euler Products and New Infinite Products for π.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Google Scholar|url=https://scholar.google.com/scholar?cites=9983115802662618115&as_sdt=2005&sciodt=0,5&hl=en|access-date=2020-06-07|website=scholar.google.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=June 19, 2009|first=Gyan|last=Prakash|title=Bihar cop in league of top mathematicians|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/patna/Bihar-cop-in-league-of-top-mathematicians/articleshow/4672385.cms|access-date=2020-06-07|website=The Times of India|language=en}}</ref>

Published "Euler Sums and Integral Connections" in MDPI.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Sofo|first=Anthony|last2=Nimbran|first2=Amrik Singh|date=2019-09-09|title=Euler Sums and Integral Connections|journal=Mathematics|volume=7|issue=9|pages=833|doi=10.3390/math7090833|issn=2227-7390|doi-access=free|url=https://vuir.vu.edu.au/45963/1/mathematics-07-00833-v2.pdf}}</ref> He has 64 publications on mathematics and he is mainly contributing in arc tangent identities, infinite series and infinite products for computing Pi.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Amrik Nimbran|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Amrik_Nimbran|access-date=2020-06-07|website=ResearchGate|language=en}}</ref>
